target_customer: Event companies, venue operators and teams running events with large mobile workforces
problem: Teams coordinating live events relied on desktop oriented tools or ad hoc texting. GoComm offered a mobile first task and communication feed with an SMS fallback when data failed.
business_model: Software subscription for event and mobile teams; pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: Mobile team communication and task management

founders.name: Travis Dredd
founders.background_notes: Listed by YC page and named by TechCrunch (2013-08-13). CB Insights lists the legal entity as Gate 5 Technologies, dba GoComm.

founders.name: John Gedmark
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: Not found; CB Insights labels the company Seed and Dead

competitors.name: Yammer
competitors.what: Enterprise social network, mainly used at desktops
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as the comparison point

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile apps with event scoped logins, a notification feed and an SMS fallback for overloaded cell networks. Standard engineering with some reliability work.

defensibility.rationale: Team messaging with task assignment was easy to copy and well funded rivals existed; the SMS fallback was the only differentiator noted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented for GoComm. A low quality directory page attributes failure to Slack, which launched publicly in 2014, but this is not reliable.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2013-08-13) said the app was tried in hotel resorts, construction, security forces and airlines, with events of thousands of attendees, but gave no usage numbers.

branding.domain_note: gocomm.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page, so the exact .com was lost or parked.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic Go plus Comm name that matches an older paging firm (GoComm Wireless) and similarly named companies; no brand assets or community found.

outcome_analysis: GoComm joined YC in Summer 2013 and moved to public beta in August 2013 with no outside funding, positioning mobile event coordination against Yammer, Chatter and Convo. The YC directory lists it as inactive and CB Insights labels it dead with about $20 thousand raised, but no post-mortem or shutdown date was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: The $20K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, undated); TechCrunch says no outside funding had been raised as of August 2013. The shutdown rests on directory status plus the CB Insights Dead label. The company site redirects to a domain for sale page and is treated as dead. A loot-drop.io page blames Slack but was judged unreliable and not used.
